walkthroughs.body_html:
Designing For Cleaner Environment — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Designing For Cleaner Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Designing For Cleaner Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: They are the same thing with different names.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.

mcqs.q: What property do shape memory alloys have?
options: They remember every shape they have ever been bent into.
They return to a pre-set shape when heated.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.
They glow when touched.

mcqs.q: Why can thermoplastics be recycled but thermosets cannot?
options: Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remoulded; thermosets have cross-links that lock the shape permanently.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Thermosets are too dangerous to recycle.
